outcome: High opioid use (defined as a mean daily opioid consumption, standardized to the postoperative length of stay (excluding the first 24 postoperative hours to account for neuraxial morphine), greater than the 75th percentile of all opioid consumption)
cohort: 949 women who underwent cesarean delivery under neuraxial anesthesia with neuraxial morphine at a single institution from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015
finding: No sociodemographic, antepartum, or intrapartum characteristics were associated with high opioid consumption after cesarean delivery.
